intent: One defect shape, five instances: a value is accepted at the boundary, a default or a cast papers over the gap, and the damage lands in a column nobody re-validates. Four came from the 2026-08-30 fresh-agent QA pass (findings 4, 5+16, 8, 14); the fifth came from driving the product in a browser, which that pass could not do.
invariants: I1 A schedule that can never fire is refused at the boundary, not stored enabled-and-dead.
I2 The refusal does not cost legitimate expressions: the 29th of February is accepted, and a day-of-month impossible for its month is still accepted when a day-of-week can match it.
I3 Only cron is judged. An interval shorthand or an ISO instant is not a cron and carries none of this problem.
I4 Two unnamed missions with different instructions get different names.
I5 A delete that deleted nothing says so. The boolean the repository already returns is not thrown away.
I6 A character written as a string is a named character, not three undefineds in the model's prompt.
I7 A 404 an operator will hit on their FIRST visit explains itself, and says whether it is normal.
the_trap_in_the_obvious_fix: Finding 4's natural fix is to call computeNextRun and refuse a null. That would refuse `0 0 29 2 *` -- a legitimate expression firing every four years -- because the prober gives up after CAP_MINUTES, 366 days. It would be a new defect wearing the old one's clothes, and it would have looked like a fix. cronCanEverFire is therefore STRUCTURAL: it intersects the day-of-month set with the longest possible month, and honours the standard cron rule that a restricted day-of-week ORs with day-of-month rather than ANDing.
what_the_existing_suite_caught_immediate: The guard was first wired into every schedule write. `every 10m` has fewer than five fields, so it was judged unfireable and refused -- and the existing schedule tests went red the moment the wiring landed. scheduleCanEverFire now parses first and judges only the cron kind. Worth recording because it is the suite catching a REGRESSION in a change whose own oracle was green: the new tests all passed while the product was broken for interval schedules.
two_answers_that_were_computed_and_disca: deleteCategory already returned false for an unknown id; the route answered 200 {deleted:id} and threw the boolean away. The correct sibling is four files over in schedules/[id]/route.ts.

The /logs route already built availableLogs before its guards. T-0071 fixed the missing-FILE 404 to carry it; the missing-DIRECTORY 404 three lines up returned a bare not-found, which the page rendered as 'No matching log files' -- indistinguishable from an empty state, on the very first visit of a fresh install.
mutation_finding: Eleven mutations, ten caught, one survivor -- and the survivor is the same seam-blindness this programme keeps finding. Stripping the body from the directory-missing 404 changed nothing observable, because every test of that path mocked the useLogs HOOK. The page tests proved the page renders an error when handed one; nothing proved the route hands one over. Fixed by driving the real handler: the 404 now asserts a reason, that the reason says a missing logs directory is NORMAL on a fresh install, and that availableLogs is still present for the page to read. One further mutation proved nothing -- its pattern did not match the file -- and was re-expressed against the derivation itself rather than a regex, then re-run. 11/11 after.
oracle_provenance: boundary-accepts-column-lies.test.ts committed alone at e8d1c77c ahead of the implementation, and the route-level additions at 6d80e8fb after mutation exposed the gap. Green controls are load-bearing throughout: Feb 29 accepted, `0 0 30 2 1` accepted (day-of-week saves it), a properly-shaped character left alone, and an existing log still served normally.
verification: Proved live on an isolated instance over HTTP: `0 0 30 2 *` and `0 0 31 4 *` refused 400 naming the reason; `0 0 29 2 *` accepted 201; `every 10m` and `0 9 * * *` accepted with real next runs; DELETE an unknown category -> 404 'Category not found'; GET /api/logs on an install with no logs directory -> 404 carrying the fresh-install explanation AND availableLogs; a mission dispatched with no name -> 'Summarise the Q3 revenue report for the board' rather than a shared constant. Gate: lint 0, tsc 0, 3520 tests / 402 suites, knip 0, canary OK, build 0.
